growing_tip.body_text: Green Onion | → Parade → Deep Purple → 5 rows (6’’-15 cm), spaced every 6” (15 cm) on the row → Green onions will do great in beds that were previously amended with compost and fertilized with a mix of alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). | → Rotary harrow → 30” bed prep rake → Popping tray and marking roller → Remove tarp and clean out large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). To make transplanting easier (seeing as the soil is loose after being harrowed), we only prepare the beds when we are about to transplant. → Pass with the dibbler-roller to mark the planting holes and bring out the well-watered trays. → Once the beds are ready, 1 person will drop the seedlings while 2 others transplant the plants as fast as possible making sure that at least 3–4 onions are dropping (if not, combine plugs). 3 people/100’bed is good ratio for efficient workflow. → Install irrigation and water until the soil is deeply moistened. * If the previous crop is too well established, or if the bed is too messy, mow the crop as low as possible and harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). Add 1’’ (2.5 cm) of compost evenly spread on the whole width of the bed and transplant into compost following a no-till strategy → 10–14days after transplanting, use the bio disc to cultivate on the row and between the rows in one single pass. → No action is required 2 → Green onions are harvested with their tops and bunched in the fields in a kneeled position. → Onions are picked when they sized up between 3-4’’ (10–12 cm). Bottoms should be white, without any dead leaves — make sure to strip off any leaves that are crushed, or have signs of rip damage. → Make bunches of +/- 9 onions by grabbing 2 clumps and tying them with a rubber band. irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (4 per bed) or sprinkler, although over head irrigation can increase foliar disease | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → General: Steady supply of moisture; if too dry, onions get a strong unpleasant flavor. Avoid water on leaves to minimize downy mildew Green onions are one of the most reliable crops. Easy to grow, consistently popular and they generate a good revenue per bed planted. We plant some every 2 weeks to ensure a constant supply throughout the season. For every seeding, we plan enough beds for an estimated 3 weeks of supply. In our planting program, green onions are grouped with crops like lettuce, rapini, bok choy, mini-romaine, mini-fennel, dill, cilantro and mini-kohlrabi — all crops that stay in the fields +/- 50 days and that have similar crop requirements. 1
